mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate at or below 0.5% (current level) is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as low rates reduce discount rates for equity valuations and stimulate economic activity.
failure_condition: In the walk-forward period, the 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals strong labor market conditions, which typically lead to higher consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When both PAYEMS and HOUST are rising, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (defined as FEDFUNDS > 1.0% and CPIAUCSL YoY inflation > 2.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to reduced liquidity and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: In the walk-forward period, during the regime defined by the trigger condition, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly real GDP growth rate (GDPC1) is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days, as stronger economic growth supports corporate earnings and investor confidence.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 is above its 5-year average, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95.0 signals weakening economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 95.0, the 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the threshold condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS are rising, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year CPI inflation rate above 3.0% signals potential monetary policy tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to higher real interest rates.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY inflation exceeds 3.0%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.
